key_insight: tttLRM uses a Test‑Time Training (TTT) layer to compress multiple image observations into fast weights, forming an implicit 3D latent representation that supports autoregressive reconstruction with linear computational complexity. This enables long‑context multi‑view 3D reconstruction that can be decoded into explicit formats like Gaussian Splats.
problem_solved: Existing multi‑view and autoregressive 3D reconstruction methods struggle to scale to long input sequences because of quadratic compute/memory growth or limited context; tttLRM addresses this by encoding observations into compact fast weights at test time to keep complexity linear while preserving reconstruction fidelity.
method: Introduce a TTT layer that stores and updates fast weights at test time to compress multiple image observations into a compact implicit 3D latent state.
Perform autoregressive decoding from the TTT latent state so reconstruction complexity grows linearly with the number of views/steps.
Decode the implicit latent into explicit downstream formats (e.g., Gaussian Splats) for rendering and application-specific use.
impact: Enables scalable, compute‑efficient 3D reconstruction from many images, making large‑context multi‑view pipelines practical for mapping, AR/VR, robotics, and other real‑world applications. Practitioners can handle longer sequences without prohibitive memory or runtime costs.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: encoder images → TTT layer (fast weights) → autoregressive decoder → explicit outputs (Gaussian Splats).
Sequence/flowchart showing how multiple views are compressed into fast weights at test time and then decoded autoregressively.
Complexity plot comparing linear (tttLRM) vs quadratic scaling (baseline) as number of views increases.
Before/after renders: input image set alongside reconstructed Gaussian Splat outputs to show qualitative gains.
paper_title: tttLRM: Test-Time Training for Long Context and Autoregressive 3D Reconstruction
paper_authors: Chen Wang, Hao Tan, Wang Yifan, Zhiqin Chen, Yuheng Liu
